label: D1 after an unrewarded trial, agent about to switch to a1
explanation: Sparse feature (0.19% of steps) that fires only at D1, almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (99.4% of mass on prev_reward==0), and only when the agent goes on to choose a1 (96% of mass). The model policy logit at D1 is always in a narrow band, about +4 to +7 toward a1. It is strongest when the agent is about to switch to a1, usually after a common a2 trial that went unrewarded (stay==0: 69% of mass, and the top quartile is 83% covered). The recorded predicate uses the agent own upcoming choice (action, stay), which counts as legitimate. It uses no future random outcome. The fully observed version, D1 & prev_reward==0 & choice logit in (4,7), covers 99% of mass but has precision 0.05. The broad condition D1 & prev_reward==0 & action==1 has recall 0.93 but precision 0.03. Adding the switch raises precision to 0.16 (dev F1 0.24, mass recall 0.69). Within this condition most steps stay silent, and no tested variable picks out which ones fire: two unrewarded trials in a row, episode position (rate peaks at trials 40-80), a narrower logit band, or a common previous transition. It never fires at GO or D2, after a rewarded trial, or before an a2 choice.
